outcome: unintended extensions of the hysterotomy during caesarean delivery
evaluation for lower urinary tract injury
cohort: 2707 women who underwent low-transverse caesarean deliveries in 2011 at an academic, tertiary-care hospital
finding: Neonatal weight, arrest of labor (both first-stage and second-stage), and non-reassuring foetal status were significantly associated with unintended hysterotomy extensions during caesarean delivery, which in turn led to increased maternal morbidity.
mod_finding: This study examines risk factors and maternal morbidity associated with unintended extensions of hysterotomy during cesarean delivery.
